thread.title: U.S. stock futures slip lower, with GE earnings on deck - MarketWatch

author: Barbara Kollmeyer
title: U.S. stock futures slip lower, with GE earnings on deck - MarketWatch
text:
U.S. stocks fell on Friday, as weakness in both energy and technology stocks offset the latest batch of corporate earnings, which continued to largely beat expectations.
Read more: Hopes are high for this earnings season—and that could prove dangerous
What are the main benchmarks doing? The Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -0.82% fell 228.27 points, or 0.9%, to 24,437. The S&P 500 SPX, -0.85% was down 25 points, or 0.9%, to 2,667. The Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, -1.27% was off 95 points to 7,141, a decline of 1.3%.
The day’s losses were widespread, with all 11 primary S&P 500 sectors down on the day, suggesting major indexes would post their second straight daily decline. However, that comes after three straight positive sessions. For the week, the Dow is up 0.4% while the S&P has gained 0.7% and the Nasdaq is up 0.8%.
What’s driving markets? As has been the case throughout the week, earnings will likely be the primary driver of sentiment, with the results gleaned for insight into the strength of American corporations at a time when questions are swirling around economic growth prospects and stock valuations. Next week will see dozens more companies report.
Oil prices shifted lower immediately after President Trump tweeted that high crude prices “will not be accepted” and that current prices were “artificially high” due to actions by the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries. That came as OPEC ministers, at a meeting, reaffirmed a commitment to keep output limited. Crude-oil futures CLK8, -0.04% were down as much as 1% earlier, but recovered to trade 0.2% lower at $68.22 a barrel, near their 3 1/5 year high set earlier in the week.
Read: Why Trump is tweeting about OPEC—and what he can do about oil prices
Investors will likely keep an eye on the 10- year Treasury note yield TMUBMUSD10Y, +1.57% which shot up to 2.94% on Thursday, the highest since Feb. 23, on rising inflation expectations .
What are strategists saying? “I think a lot of people are clueless about what the next $10 move will be for oil, whether it will be up or down, and this adds to the level of uncertainty in the market, which was already pretty high,” said Chris Bertelsen, chief investment officer of Aviance Capital Management.
That said, he added, “I know they’re dramatic, but I tend to ignore Trump’s tweets. You never know when he’s going to say something, or if there will be something behind his words” that will result in a policy change. “Meanwhile, earnings continue to come in strong and suggest that valuations are supported.”

See also: Here’s why small-cap stocks could be vulnerable to ETF outflows
What stocks are in focus? GE GE, +3.93% shares rose 3.4% after it reported adjusted earnings ahead of Wall Street forecasts, and reaffirmed its guidance. Despite the gain, the industrial conglomerate remains the worst performing Dow component over the past year, a period over which it has shed about 50% of its value.
Baker Hughes BHGE, +0.83% reported adjusted earnings that topped expectations , but revenue that was slightly under forecasts. The stock rose 2.9%.
Apple Inc . AAPL, -4.10% tumbled 4% after a pair of analysts issued cautious notes ahead of the company’s second-quarter earnings report, due out in early May. The stock was one of the biggest drags on the overall market.
Honeywell International Inc. HON, +1.65% rose 0.4% after reporting its first-quarter results and raising its outlook.
Schlumberger Ltd. SLB, -1.49% fell 2%. The oil giant topped earnings estimates , but said it expects the sector to see supply challenges this year.
Atlassian Corp. PLC TEAM, -6.53% shares fell 7.6% after the software maker reported earnings late Thursday.
State Street Corp. STT, -4.34% STT, -4.34% fell 4.1% despite better-than-expected earnings and revenue .
Twitter Inc. TWTR, +1.17% shares rose 1.3% after MKM Partners lifted shares to buy from neutral .

Pivotal Software Inc. PVTL, +4.87% rose 2.5% in its trading debut, after its initial public offering was priced at $15 a share. The cloud-software company is majority controlled by Dell Technologies Inc. and VMware Inc . VMW, +0.34%
See: Pivotal IPO—5 things to know about the cloud software company
What are other markets doing? European stocks SXXP, -0.03% shook off earlier losses to move higher . Asian markets CLK8, -0.04% finished lower, as chip-related stocks got hit .
Gold futures GCM8, -0.79% moved south, while the ICE U.S. Dollar Index DXY, +0.44% climbed to an 11-day high , boosted partially by higher Treasury yields. The U.K. pound GBPUSD, -0.4758% fell after Bank of England Gov. Mark Carney dampened expectations for an interest-rate hike in May.
